column4: Visit note | 2025-12-10 10:30 AM | Dr. Farhana Kabir, General Medicine | Patient: Popy Rahman, 24, female. Ms. Rahman presents for review regarding her brittle nails and getting breathless on the stairs. She explains that her symptoms worsened after a long spell of poor meals while living alone in Rangpur. She is employed as a garment factory worker. She reports that her fatigue makes long shifts difficult. She has Essential hypertension. Relevant negatives include no fever, chest pain, or bleeding gums. On examination: haemoglobin 8.1 g/dL, BP 152/89 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, weight 92 kg. Conjunctivae are pale, and heart sounds are normal without murmurs. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued for her condition. She was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and to avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin test.
